name: Catholicism
summary: Catholicism, as a political ideology, is the body of Catholic social teaching: it holds that society rests on the dignity of the human person, the family, subsidiarity, solidarity and a common good bound by natural law. It defends private property as a natural right while subordinating it to the universal destination of goods, endorses unions and a just wage, criticises both socialism and unregulated capitalism, and opposes abortion, euthanasia, the death penalty and same-sex marriage. It rejects totalitarianism and holds that the Church is distinct from, yet may judge, the political community.
scope: Catholic social teaching from Leo XIII's Rerum Novarum (1891) through the Second Vatican Council's Dignitatis humanae, John Paul II's Centesimus annus and the Catechism of the Catholic Church, with Wikipedia's overview for later popes. It excludes Catholic integralist or monarchist movements, Christian democratic parties as organisations, liberation theology, and the Church's internal doctrine except where it shapes public positions. Many answers on technology, finance and institutions are inferred and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Catholic social teaching holds that the state must see that workers and the vulnerable have security, and Centesimus annus backs support for the unemployed and social security; healthcare itself is inferred from this.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rerum Novarum demands a wage sufficient to support a frugal worker and his family and lets public authority step in, which adherents read as backing wage floors; the minimum wage is not named.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Centesimus annus grants the market is an efficient allocator but only for needs with purchasing power, and the Catechism says many human needs cannot be met by the market.

public-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private property and condemns state or communal ownership as the remedy, though the state may regulate ownership; strategic public utilities are not excluded in later teaching.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Church teaches that political authority may regulate property for the common good and that owners are stewards, but it prescribes no tax rates and adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum Novarum calls workers' unions the most important of all associations and urges their growth, and later popes repeat the endorsement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats private property as a natural right and its inviolability as basic, but the Catechism subordinates it to the universal destination of goods, so it can be overridden for the common good.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Catechism commends reasonable regulation of economic life and says profit cannot be the sole norm; Centesimus annus says the market must not be the only reference point.

cut-welfare.rationale: Centesimus annus supports social security and minimum support for the unemployed and Catholic teaching gives priority to the poor, while it also warns against a state that crowds out subsidiarity.

worker-ownership.rationale: Catholic teaching encourages wide ownership and worker participation (partnership, associations) but never makes collective worker ownership of firms a requirement; adherents split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Church accepts that authorities may defend the community against unjust aggressors but sets no doctrine on surveillance; inferred as split between security and privacy and dignity concerns.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the sources consulted; inferred from the Catechism's stress on protecting life and health and on authority's duty to the common good, which makes legalisation unwelcome.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Church condemns hatred and unjust discrimination but sets no rule on legal speech limits, and Dignitatis humanae warns against arbitrary state action; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Authority is a service bound by natural law and human rights, and Centesimus annus condemns authoritarian regimes; bypassing checks runs against that.

state-harmful.rationale: Catholic teaching holds that political authority comes from the order of creation and the state has a duty to protect the common good, so anarchism is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the Church backs authority's duty of protection and legitimate defence but takes no stance on gun regulation.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Catechism accepts legitimate defence by authorities but also criticises arms races; no doctrine on funding levels.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Catechism calls prostitution always gravely sinful, a reduction of persons to instruments, and civil authority is expected to defend morality of this kind.

decide-locally.rationale: Subsidiarity, named by Centesimus annus as a guiding principle, assigns tasks to the lowest competent level, though the Church also supports larger bodies where needed.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Catechism says penalties should have a corrective as well as a protective purpose and calls the death penalty inadmissible, while retaining proportionate punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Rerum Novarum and the Catechism treat the family as a natural society prior to the state and marriage between man and woman as sacramental and foundational.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Catechism holds that homosexual acts cannot be approved and defines marriage as an indissoluble union ordered to children; the Church opposes legal same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Catechism says life is to be protected absolutely from conception, direct abortion is gravely wrong, and civil law should protect the unborn child.

more-religion-public.rationale: Dignitatis humanae asks government to favour the religious life of citizens and the Catechism says the Church judges political matters when needed, but without coercion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Church affirms equal dignity and condemns discrimination, but historic-redress policy is not a doctrine and adherents split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Catechism's natural-law framing of sexuality and marriage as ordered to male-female complementarity; the specific claim is not addressed in the pages opened.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Catechism says immigrants should respect the heritage of their host nation and Catholic teaching values national cultural heritage, within a universal outlook.

gradual-change.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours reform through justice and cooperation rather than upheaval and Catholic social teaching respects established institutions and the family as prior to the state.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Catechism says richer nations should welcome foreigners as far as they are able, though authorities may set legal conditions for the common good.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pacem in terris, as described in the overview, calls for a stronger United Nations, and Paul VI urged obligations of rich states to poor ones.

free-trade.rationale: Paul VI, per the overview, argued free trade alone cannot remedy global disparities, and Centesimus annus refuses to treat the market as the sole guide.

nation-first.rationale: Catholic social teaching stresses solidarity among peoples and duties of rich nations to the poor, so putting national interest ahead of cooperation is rejected, though patriotism is valued.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Catechism accepts that authorities may use force in legitimate defence of communities under strict conditions; intervention for rights is an extension that Catholic thinkers debate.

open-borders.rationale: The Church urges welcome to migrants but the Catechism explicitly allows legal conditions on entry for the common good, so open borders are not required.

limit-growth.rationale: Laudato si' criticises consumerism and the Church treats economic life as subordinate to human good, but Catholic teaching supports development and rejects limiting growth as a goal; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Francis's Laudato si', as summarised, calls for global action on environmental degradation and climate change.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching that material progress cannot replace moral and spiritual ends and Centesimus annus's critique of a life of having over being.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; the Church opposes nuclear weapons but has no doctrine on nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects class struggle and seeks reform by justice; Centesimus annus praises non-violent change in 1989 though the Church admits resistance to tyranny in extremis.

experts-over-public.rationale: Subsidiarity and participation point against rule by experts, but the Church does not address technocracy directly; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Centesimus annus and the Catechism condemn systems that subordinate individual rights to collective production and reject collectivism.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Church accepts markets within a moral and legal frame but promotes broad private ownership; it does not require worker or public ownership as a condition.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not addressed; Catholic teaching defends private property rights and allows regulation, so replacing most taxes with a single land tax is not part of it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats inheritance and bequest as part of the natural property right, and the Catechism lists inheritance as a legitimate means of acquisition.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; teaching on just wages and support for the unemployed gives mixed signals, and adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Catholic teaching has no tariff doctrine; concern for workers and for poor countries pulls in opposite directions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Subsidiarity says the state should create conditions for economic activity rather than direct it, per Centesimus annus.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rerum Novarum wants as many workers as possible to become owners, and the Catechism says productive goods should serve as many people as possible.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends wages and private property and rejects the abolition of ownership.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic teaching accepts regulation of economic life and does not endorse free banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rerum Novarum and later teaching favour associations of workers and employers cooperating, though state-compelled bodies setting prices go beyond what the sources say.

one-party-rule.rationale: Centesimus annus condemns totalitarian and authoritarian regimes and the Catechism rejects totalitarian ideologies.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Catholic teaching does not prescribe a regime and has accepted monarchies historically; the Catechism says authority must be legitimate and serve the common good.

democracy-best.rationale: Centesimus annus welcomes democratic participation and rights, while the Church holds that majorities are bound by natural law and human dignity, so it is cautious about 'even when voters choose badly'.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from teaching on common good, authority and representation which does not favour plebiscitary government.

workers-councils.rationale: Rerum Novarum and Centesimus annus reject class-based rule and the subordination of persons to collectives; political power rests on the common good, not worker bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; the Church speaks of the rights of peoples but gives no doctrine on secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Catholic teaching holds persons equal in dignity but accepts that authority is natural to society; inferred, with the stress on service rather than superiority.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Church condemns violence and praised non-violent change, but accepts legitimate defence by authorities, so 'never' is too absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Centesimus annus says peace is never merely a result of military victory, and the Catechism calls peace the work of justice and charity.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Church distinguishes itself from the political community but Dignitatis humanae asks governments to show favour to religious life and allows recognition of one religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic social teaching bases law on natural law knowable by reason and not on scripture directly, though it holds that law should not contradict it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Catechism gives public authority the duty of justice, penalties and defence of the community, so privatising them is outside Catholic teaching.

military-superiority.rationale: The Catechism criticises the arms race as a grave threat and treats peace as justice, so seeking superiority over rivals is not endorsed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Catholic teaching affirms the equal dignity of all and a universal community, and the Catechism asks hosts to welcome immigrants.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum Novarum says class conflict is not natural and Centesimus annus condemns class struggle in the Marxist sense.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Church teaches equal dignity and priority to the poor, but accepts differences of property and rank and rejects levelling by abolishing ownership.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in sources opened; the Church supports the rights of peoples and the poor yet gives no doctrine on indigenous authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; the Church urges rich countries to meet duties to poor ones but gives no teaching on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Church favours solidarity between peoples, but union on religious or civilisational lines is not part of its teaching; adherents split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Catechism says profit cannot be the sole norm and 'You cannot serve God and mammon', and Centesimus annus criticises a life oriented to having.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Church teaches both rights grounded in dignity and duties, and the Catechism says authorities must respect fundamental rights, so rights are not subordinated to duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Laudato si' stresses care for creation, but the Church grounds nature's value in God and human stewardship; split on 'apart from usefulness'.

limit-population.rationale: The Catechism says the state may inform citizens on demography but may not use coercion, and calls contraceptive acts intrinsically evil.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Catholic social teaching arose to reform industrial society, not abolish it, and Rerum Novarum accepts industry with just treatment of labour.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the stress on stability, subsidiarity and a human-centred economy; disruption of institutions for its own sake is not endorsed.

human-enhancement.rationale: The Catechism rejects manipulation of embryos and treats persons as images of God; enhancement is inferred as disfavoured.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from teaching that authority is a service by persons answerable to natural law and the common good.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed in Catholic teaching; adherents split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Catholic teaching does not seek a return to a past order as such; Centesimus annus engages with the modern world and Dignitatis humanae revised older positions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Catholic social teaching presents itself as principles rooted in natural law, not a pragmatic test, but the Church says it is not an ideology; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours legal association and cooperation, and Centesimus annus praises non-violent change through society, not rejection of institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Catechism says the Church uses only means consistent with the Gospel and Centesimus annus praises non-violence; the statement is inferred as broadly congenial.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Catholic social teaching builds on work, property and civilisation and treats these as natural; nothing supports abandoning them.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts varied tasks and ranks in society as natural and calls for cooperation of capital and labour, not the end of differing roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The universal destination of goods and priority to the poor point toward need, but the Church also endorses just wages by work and private property, so adherents are split.

production-for-use.rationale: The Church says profit cannot be the exclusive norm but accepts it as a regulator of business, per Centesimus annus; neither side fully fits.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rerum Novarum condemns exploiting workers and Centesimus annus values profit as a signal of a healthy firm, so profit as such is not exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Church rejects Marxist class struggle and totalitarian regimes.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects collective ownership of land and defends private property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Catholic teaching criticises capitalism's individualism and idolatry of money but does not hold war to follow from it inevitably.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Catechism says political authority may regulate property for the common good and citizens owe contributions to society, so taxation is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Catholic teaching holds that law can promote the common good and morality, such as restricting pornography, beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Church teaches that the family has rights prior to the state and recognises religious communities' rights, per Rerum Novarum and Dignitatis humanae.

conscription.rationale: The Catechism accepts that authorities may require national service and respects conscientious objection, but views differ among adherents.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The Church emphasises political participation and a duty to vote (Catechism 2240) and says nothing that makes exit the main check.

state-as-business.rationale: The Catechism says authority is service and Centesimus annus says the market must not be the only reference of social life; treating citizens as customers contradicts both.

positive-liberty.rationale: Centesimus annus lists the material goods and security a just society should provide, and the universal destination of goods ties freedom to access to means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; adherents split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Church teaches the equal dignity of all persons and that there should be no discrimination among citizens, and it opposes racism.

organic-representation.rationale: Rerum Novarum and Quadragesimo anno stress families and occupational associations as intermediate bodies, and subsidiarity values them, though the Church does not require abolishing parties.

total-state.rationale: Centesimus annus condemns totalitarianism and Rerum Novarum limits the state, saying it cannot absorb the family.

national-rebirth.rationale: Catholic teaching offers moral renewal but not a radical national rebirth; the Church distances itself from fascist movements.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Catechism treats peace as the work of justice and sets strict conditions on force; expansion for its own sake is not just.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Catholic teaching says authority serves the common good, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum condemns exploiting workers and treats workers as persons with rights and dignity.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Church holds universal moral truths knowable by reason, which a power-based theory of knowledge denies.

universal-morality.rationale: The Catechism holds that no one can command what is contrary to the natural law and Dignitatis humanae grounds rights in human nature.

single-common-good.rationale: The common good is a central concept: the state has a duty to watch over it, and the Church teaches a good worked out by reason and shared, not just a balance of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Church has not framed this as doctrine; the sources set out no position, and views among Catholics vary.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in Catholic teaching; the Church urges welcome for migrants but gives no doctrine on diaspora return.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in Catholic teaching; adherents split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker participation is encouraged but the sources do not endorse democratic votes on company management; adherents split.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rerum Novarum and the Catechism hold that parents have primary responsibility for children and the state must not usurp them, which Catholic bodies apply to choice of school.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed in Catholic teaching; adherents split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Centesimus annus values economic initiative within a legal and ethical frame but does not say political freedom depends on it; adherents split.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Catechism asks leaders to practice justice and not place personal interest above the common good, while also upholding law and penalties.

national-self-determination.rationale: Catholic teaching defends the rights of peoples and of nations in the order of solidarity; the idea is inferred, not examined in the sources.

force-without-un.rationale: The Church favours a stronger UN, but the Catechism lets authorities use defence; no teaching settles unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Church holds that faith and reason complement each other and Dignitatis humanae treats faith as free assent; reason alone is not the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Church calls for protecting immigrants as vulnerable workers and for priority to the poor, so excluding them from welfare is disfavoured.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Catholic teaching values work but also calls for support for the unemployed; adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum Novarum says capital and labour need each other and class is not a natural enemy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Church values inherited cultural heritage and Centesimus annus criticises forgetting tradition; sacrificing it is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; the Church urges solidarity and fairness between nations but not a bloc against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects class conflict and Centesimus annus condemns Marxist class struggle; the Church's outlook is universal rather than a national working class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Church holds distinct but equal vocations in marriage and family but does not prescribe distinct legal roles in public life; adherents split.

ban-interest.rationale: Nothing in the Catechism's social doctrine or Centesimus annus forbids lending at interest, so a legal ban is not current teaching; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Church teaches that there should be no discrimination among citizens and affirms equal dignity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rerum Novarum says the state should protect the rights of every class, not serve one.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Laudato si' calls for global climate action and a shift away from environmentally damaging activity; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Catechism says immigrants should respect the host country's heritage and laws but does not demand giving up their culture, so adherents split on full assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Catholic teaching calls for welcoming migrants and rejects racial theories; the replacement claim has no basis in it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; electoral systems are matters of prudence.

national-mission.rationale: The Church's mission is spiritual and distinct from political power; Catechism 2245 says it must not be confused with the political community.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Church affirms the equal dignity of women and men but rejects a model of systematic male advantage as a structural account; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Catechism warns leaders against putting personal interest over the common good, but the Church offers no general claim that elites are corrupt; adherents split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Catechism says human life must be protected from conception and condemns coercion in family planning, and the state may not usurp the spouses' initiative.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Catechism asks authorities to respect human rights and justice; accountability is inferred from that.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum and Centesimus annus give the state duties to protect workers, the poor and the common good beyond defence and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Church teaches equal dignity and condemns discrimination, and marriage rests on consent.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Dignitatis humanae and Catholic social teaching ground rights in human dignity common to all, with no discrimination among citizens.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Church rejects socialism and so does not take a side in the internal Marxist debate; it leans against the premise.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Church defends freedom of religious communities and the family's priority over the state, so it favours religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Dignitatis humanae says no one is to be forced to embrace the faith and religious freedom is a right, though proselytising must avoid coercion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic teaching has no religious ban on cattle slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Parents have primary responsibility for education and the state must not usurp them, and Dignitatis humanae asks government to favour religious life.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Church rejects totalitarian states and the Marxist doctrine behind this thesis.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority is legitimate through service of the common good and respect for rights, and Centesimus annus welcomes democratic participation; explicit consent is not the sole ground.

population-transfer.rationale: The Church holds every person's dignity and rights and the Catechism asks for welcome to those seeking security; forced removal of minorities is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Catechism allows proportionate penalties and legitimate defence by public authority, so force by authority is permitted, while the Church stresses peace.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Centesimus annus values the market but treats solidarity as a cornerstone, and Rerum Novarum calls for cooperation between classes.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; the Church condemns totalitarian ideologies but gives no doctrine on banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Catholic teaching on authority as service gives partial affinity.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on authority bound by natural law and rights and on subsidiarity and limits to the state.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Church rejects Marxism and totalitarian ideology; Centesimus annus condemns the imposed view of reality of such regimes.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The preferential option for the poor is a core principle, and Rerum Novarum says the poor have a claim to special consideration.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; wide ownership is favoured but the specific policy is not.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts that strikes disrupt order but wants the laws to remove the causes, and the Church supports unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Church locates poverty in social and economic structures and injustice and rejects coercive population control.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Church welcomes migrants and stresses unity across peoples; the claim is rejected in tendency though integration is valued.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from authority as a service by those fit to exercise it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Catechism says political rights cannot be suspended without legitimate and proportionate reasons, a limit that adherents apply strictly.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; the state may regulate the economy for the common good but the sources set no stance on price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Church rejects totalitarianism and holds that no human power may compel conscience.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rejects one-party control of the state, which is condemned as totalitarian.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Catechism lets authorities set conditions for immigrants but asks for welcome; no specific teaching on waiting periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Church values the conscience of citizens and the duty to vote responsibly, so binding discipline is not endorsed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Church supports stronger international bodies (Pacem in terris); inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; forms of government are left to prudence.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Church's own government is episcopal under the pope; this is a defining feature of Catholic ecclesiology.

clerical-rule.rationale: Catechism 2245 says the Church must not be confused with the political community, and its mission is distinct from political authorities.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Church teaches duties of citizens and legitimate defence, and does not support revolutionary defeatism; Rerum Novarum rejects class war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Catechism asks civil authorities to prevent pornography as a grave offense, but general censorship of art is not Catholic doctrine; adherents split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; the Church leaves constitutional design to prudence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; the Church favours peace and cooperation but sets no doctrine on alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours widespread ownership, not a ban on renting, and defends property rights including leasing out.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Catechism accepts organised national defence by authorities; replacing the army by an armed citizenry is not taught.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Catholic teaching values the family farm and widespread ownership but no doctrine says rural life is morally better; adherents split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed in teaching on peoples' rights.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Church holds universal moral truths and that Christ's revelation is true, so it does not treat all cultures as equal, while respecting each people's dignity.

death-penalty.rationale: The Catechism (2267) says the death penalty is inadmissible as an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person and that the Church works for its abolition.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Parents have the primary responsibility for children and the state must not usurp them, and the Catechism teaches chastity; school curricula on gender equality as described are disfavoured.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Catholic teaching does not require creationism in public schools; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Catechism 2354 calls pornography a grave offense and says civil authorities should prevent its production and distribution.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; the Church's welcome to migrants and equal dignity point against exclusive descent rules.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the Church's support for the rights of peoples and the poor and for the dignity of minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Dignitatis humanae says no one should be forced to act against conscience in religious matters and that civil power should not command or prohibit religious acts.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Church values fidelity to tradition and moral truth; the statement is inferred as opposed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Catholic teaching urges relief for poor countries, but the details split adherents.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed in sources opened; Catholic development teaching ties justice to economic structures but not specifically to independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; the Church leaves constitutional method to prudence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Political rights cannot be suspended without legitimate and proportionate reasons, and Centesimus annus condemns authoritarian regimes.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Paul VI called on rich nations to meet obligations to poor ones and the Catechism asks wealthier nations to welcome foreigners and share.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The Catechism criticises the arms race and Pacem in terris denounces the nuclear arms race.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; forms of government are left to prudence.

missingStatements.text: Human life should be legally protected from conception to natural death.
missingStatements.rationale: The Catechism says life must be protected absolutely from conception and that civil law should protect the unborn, while also rejecting euthanasia.

missingStatements.text: Workers should be paid a wage sufficient to support a family.
missingStatements.rationale: Rerum Novarum says wages must not be insufficient to support a frugal worker and his family.

missingStatements.text: Higher bodies should not take over what smaller communities and families can do for themselves.
missingStatements.rationale: Subsidiarity is named by Centesimus annus as a guiding principle of the state's role, and the Catechism says the state may not usurp the spouses' initiative.

missingStatements.text: Each marriage act should remain open to the transmission of life, and artificial contraception should be rejected.
missingStatements.rationale: Catechism 2366 and 2370 call contraceptive acts intrinsically evil and require acts to stay open to life.
missingStatements.declined: A doctrinal question about private sexual morality rather than a general political position; traditional-family and abortion-legal capture the political side.

notes: Positions on sexual ethics, life and marriage are doctrine for Catholics; Catholic voters and Christian democratic parties differ widely on policy application. Positions that changed: Dignitatis humanae (1965) accepts religious freedom and the Catechism now calls the death penalty inadmissible (2267).
